chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr and al-Hajjāl, from Thal'abah ibn Maymūn, from Ma'mar ibn 'Uthmān, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about whom the clothing is obligatory in the expiation of the oath. He said: A garment that covers his 'awrah (private parts).
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the clothing used in expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the clothing required for the expiation of an oath must be sufficient to cover the 'awrah, emphasizing the principle of modesty in ritual acts. This ruling aligns with the general fiqh requirement that kaffarah items be of practical use and dignity, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the functional adequacy of the garment rather than its material value. The specification ensures that the expiation serves its purpose of honoring the oath through a tangible, respectable act.
